name: WI-04
label: Safe D

key_factors: Incumbent Gwen Moore running for reelection with over $1M raised
Republican challenger Tim Rogers has no reported fundraising
Prediction markets price Moore's win probability near 97%
model.rationale: Milwaukee-based WI-04 leans Democratic by 26 points, and incumbent Gwen Moore is running again with a large fundraising edge over a challenger who has reported no money. Markets price her near certain to win, so the forecast stays at a roughly 27-point Democratic margin.
model.watch: A surprise scandal or an unexpectedly well-funded challenger could narrow the margin, though not plausibly the likely winner.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
Gwen Moore has held this Milwaukee-area House seat since 2005, and the district's partisan lean of 26 points Democratic makes it one of the safest Democratic seats in Wisconsin. She is running for another term and raised just over $1 million for the cycle, though she reports relatively little cash on hand late in the race.

Her Republican opponent, Tim Rogers, has no reported fundraising or cash on hand, and no outside groups are spending in the district. No public polls cover the general election, but prediction markets put Moore's win chances around 97 percent. The fundamentals, incumbency, and money all point the same direction, making this a Safe Democratic seat with a wide expected margin.
